title: DeepSeek V4.1 Runs Locally, but the Fine-Tune Did Not Ship
description: Working title, draft B: yesterday's release runs V4.1 locally; the fine-tune did not ship; train what fits tonight.
hook_text: The DeepSeek fine-tune you want is a two-hundred-thirty-three-gigabyte download.
hook_candidates: Three moves and your fine-tuned Llama runs tonight.
The DeepSeek fine-tune you want sits on a two-hundred-thirty-three-gigabyte download.
You watched DeepSeek V4.1 land. The fine-tune did not.
Unsloth shipped V4.1 support. Support means running.
Just 3GB of VRAM trains a model tonight.
Fifty-five-two billion parameters. About sixteen wake per word.
You want your own DeepSeek. Tonight you train Llama.
Your card can't fine-tune V4.1. Nothing can.
Yesterday's beta runs DeepSeek V4.1 in 125 GB.
Stop waiting for a V4.1 fine-tune that isn't coming.
narration_full: The DeepSeek fine-tune you want is a two-hundred-thirty-three-gigabyte download. Yesterday, Unsloth shipped a beta whose headline is DeepSeek V four point one running locally. You watched it land wanting your own copy, fine-tuned, meaning retrained on your examples. Here is what changes for you. Park the Engram table, a giant lookup memory, on your S S D. Then V four point one runs in about one hundred twenty-five gigabytes of memory. Picture a library. The Engram table is the basement archive; each word pages up only the rows it needs. The limit: the reading room alone still overflows any gaming card. The model holds five hundred fifty-two billion parameters. It is a mixture of experts: a router wakes only a few specialist blocks per word. And memory bills you for the whole model, not the slice that fires. Here is the honest part: in this release, support means running. No fine-tuning recipe, no notebook, no training checkpoint shipped for V four point one. Unsloth's own guide points its training advice at other models. V four point one even ships without a chat template, the rules that shape your prompts. Support, it turns out, is a spectator sport. So tonight, run Unsloth's stock Q LoRA recipe. That is thin LoRA adapters trained on a four-bit compressed copy of a model that fits your card. It runs on the free tier of Colab. Load a four-bit Llama checkpoint and attach the adapters. Train on your question-and-answer dataset, save the adapter, and export to guff, the file Ollama runs. If a V four point one training path ever ships, this same recipe inherits it. Tonight, you train the model that fits your card.
